text:
sara: Heads-up - after last night's kernel-selector roll (deploy 2026-03-17T03:40 UTC) we see a ~12% drop in prefix/prompt cache hit-rate on the gpu-prod pool and a correlated spike in GPU mem pressure + a few OOM throttles. Dumping the short profiling snapshot below.

leo: link to the perf dashboard? (can you paste the KV stats?)

sara: https://dash.redwood.io/d/q/kv/prefix-hitrate?panel=3  snapshot: overall hit_rate 0.68 -> 0.56, median latency +9ms, eviction_rate x3, avg_kv_entries/GPU 1.4M -> 1.9M

anita: which kernel change landed? I remember PR #2412 swapped default kernel path for short-seq to fast-attn-v2 (kernel chooses different pad normalization). Could that change canonical keys? :thinking_face:

dylan: quick hypothesis: kernel-specific padding/sequence-normalization changed the serialized prompt that's used in the KV key. If keys differ even by trailing pad bytes we lose prefix hits and warmup prefills become useless -> more cold misses and memory churn.

perf-bench-bot: automated-sample: 2026-03-17T04:00Z
kv_cache: baseline_hit_rate: 0.68, post_rollout_hit_rate: 0.56, eviction_count: 18240, avg_slots_per_gpu: 1900123, warmup_fill_time_p95: 1.2s -> 2.7s, oom_count: 6

sara: confirmed we see more unique key prefixes in the heatmap. attaching short dump (trimmed). Also saw increased fragmentation in slab allocs on GPU.

leo: we should check the key-serialization codepath for any kernel-dependent bits. Also verify that the canonicalizer (lowercasing + whitespace trim) is applied at the same point for all paths.

anita: noted - the kernel change moved tokenization normalization earlier in the pipeline for perf reasons. I suspected no-one changed the canonicalizer, but if tokenization produces a different whitespace pattern the final key will diverge. I'll diff the serialization output for a few representative prompts.

dylan: mitigation plan suggestion - two quick sims: 1) run an offline replay on canary cluster where we compute "canonicalized_key_v2" that strips pad tokens and normalizes case/whitespace; compare hit rate. 2) adjust eviction soft-cap + soft-ttl to give more time for warmup prefills while we investigate.

sara: immediate temporary mitigation I'm proposing: increase softcap by +15% on gpu-prod and lengthen soft-ttl from 20s -> 45s for routes with high reuse. That should reduce eviction churn and OOMs while we validate canonicalization.

perf-bench-bot: queued canary job: replay_kv_keys --source=prod-sample-20260316 --canonicalizer=strip-pads-v1 --out=canary-report.json  ETA 18m

anita: I ran a small diff against 1000 prompts. Result: ~9% of keys differ because tokenization now emits a trailing pad marker for short sequences. Example: old_serialized: "prompt|user:...|len:12" new_serialized: "prompt|user:...|len:12|PAD" So canonicalizer must strip PAD markers (they're not semantically meaningful) before hashing.

leo: let's make the canonicalizer kernel-aware or, better, move canonicalization to run after tokenization normalization so it sees the canonical token stream and strips pad markers regardless of kernel.

dylan: small optimization: instead of changing the global canonicalizer immediately, we can add a shim that normalizes keys for the new kernel path only and roll it as config; then measure hit-rate delta.

sara: agreed. roll steps: 1) shimming change + canary (config flag for fast-attn-v2 keys) - monitor hit_rate, eviction_count, p95 warmup time. target improvement: hit_rate +8% within 1h. 2) if good, move canonicalization to post-tokenization and add unit tests that normalize pad tokens, case, and trailing whitespace. 3) experiment with soft-ttl and softcap permanent tuning: run parameter sweep offline to find knee (we saw +15% softcap +45s TTL reduced eviction_rate by ~40% in a synthetic replay).

perf-bench-bot: canary job finished: canary_hit_rate: 0.66 (vs 0.56 post-rollout), eviction_rate: -35%, warmup_p95: 1.4s. Seems the shim regained a lot of hits but not all.

anita: pushing hotfix PR to strip pad tokens in key canonicalizer: git push origin key-canonicalize-fix -> PR 2458. Small note: adding this change increases canonicalizer CPU by ~0.8% in microbench but reduces network/GPU churn so net win.

leo: good. after PR merges let's tune batching heuristics too: kernel selection changed batching decisions (fast-attn-v2 favors higher batch_size for throughput) which increases the KV footprint per step. We should cap batch_size for high-reuse routes or prefer latency-optimized kernel for short prompts.

sara: agree - add policy: if route.hit_rate > 0.6 prefer latency kernel or cap batch_size_for_route <= 8. Add to rollout plan.

dylan: also let's run frag compaction job on impacted GPU nodes during low-traffic window. Compaction should reclaim slab space and reduce OOM frequency.

sara: plan timeline: - now: enable softcap + soft-ttl on prod (sara) - +20m: canary shim validated -> merge PR 2458 (anita) - +1h: kernel-aware batching policy rollout to 10% of traffic (leo) - +6h: observe metrics, run compaction job overnight (dylan)

everyone: pls react with :thumbsup: if you agree or flag concerns.

leo: :+1: will add metric checks in the SLO dashboard and create alert if hit_rate falls below 0.6 or OOM > 2 in 15m.

anita: :thumbsup: merging PR now.

perf-bench-bot: alert scheduled: monitor/kv/prefix-hitrate (threshold 0.6) -> notify #eng-runtime on breach.

sara: thanks all - keeping thread open for results. If fix doesn't fully restore behavior we'll need to re-evaluate kernel selection heuristics and consider reverting the selector temporarily.
